cards.explanation: The question is, “Where is the good way?” The LORD even hands everyone the words: “Ask for the ancient paths: ‘Where is the good way?’…” Then comes the promise, “Then walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls.”

The answer is False. The text says, “…‘We will not walk in it!’” That's like your GPS saying turn left and you answering out loud that you will not. The LORD shows them the good way, and they refuse it.

The answer is that they refuse to listen. The LORD says, “I appointed watchmen over you and said, ‘Listen for the sound of the ram’s horn.’…” Their answer: “We will not listen!” That's somebody telling the smoke alarm in advance to hush. The LORD gives them a warning to listen for, and they turn away from it.

The LORD calls on the nations and the whole earth. He says, “Therefore hear, O nations, and learn, O congregations, what will happen to them.” Then He adds, “Hear, O earth!” That's a call for everybody to listen in.

The reason He gives is that they rejected His instruction. The LORD says the disaster comes “…because they have paid no attention to My word and have rejected My instruction.” He also calls it “…the fruit of their own schemes…” That's the reason He gives, and I'll stick with it, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please Me.” Those are plain words, and I won't dress them up, friends. The people's offerings do not please Him.

The answer is that they will perish, and it's a heavy line. The LORD says, “fathers and sons alike will be staggered; friends and neighbors will perish.” I think this part is hard to read. It's a serious word, so I'll just let it stand.

The LORD describes them as cruel and merciless. He says, “They grasp the bow and spear; they are cruel and merciless.” Then He adds that “Their voice roars like the sea…” It's a heavy picture, and I'll just let the words stand, friends.
The answer is False. The cry is, “We have heard the report; our hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped us…” Nobody is lacing up their boots here, friends. They hear the news and their hands drop.

The answer is True. The warning says, “Do not go out to the fields; do not walk the road.” The reason is right there with it: “For the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side.” The warning and its reason sit side by side in the same verse.

The reason is that the destroyer will come suddenly. The verse says to mourn “…for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.” The mourning is compared to what you'd do “…for an only son…” It's a heavy picture, and I'd be careful not to rush past it, friends.

The missing word is rebels. The LORD says, “All are hardened rebels, walking around as slanderers.” He goes on, “They are bronze and iron; all of them are corrupt.” Hardened is a strong word, and it's His.

The answer is False. The verse says, “The bellows blow fiercely, blasting away the lead with fire.” Then it adds, “The refining proceeds in vain, for the wicked are not purged.” All that fire, and the wicked aren't purged.

The answer is rejected silver, and it's a heavy word. The verse says, “They are called rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them.” I think this one is hard to read, so I'll just let it sit for a moment, friends.
